newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says copper costs about 70 cts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says copper costs about 70 cts.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Friday that the group's operating costs for copper was now about 70 U.S. cents a pound.

Managing director John Prescott told reporters at a briefing after the release of first half results that the company, the world's second largest copper producer, was targetting further falls in operating costs.
"We are targetting another six cents there (North America) specific to the North American operations -- and a further five cents across the board," Prescott said.
Asked what the group's current operating costs were for copper, he replied: "We are just above 70 cents now."

The costs in the North American operations, which consist of the Magma Copper operations acquired at the start of 1996, would be brought down to about 60 U.S. cents per poiund "or a shade better" after the further six cent reduction.
Prescott added that across-the-board the operating cost would fall to significantly below 50 U.S. cents if the targetted reductions were met.
BHP is the majority owner of the Escondida copper project in Chile. RTZ/CRA is its partner.

Prescott declined to give a specific forecast of the copper price but said "generally we think that there will be some firming pressure in (calendar) 1997 but we are not building that into our numbers yet."
BHP's operating cost for copper in North America was about 85 U.S. cents a pound in the 1996/97 first quarter.
